body:
I'm not sure the call to `_setup_local_to_scene()` should be happening anyway because you're not instantiating anything.  Sometimes when I was working on this, that print statement stopped happening and I needed begin again with a fresh copy of your mrp project.  

If what you were doing was right, then changing the `extends ViewportTexture` to `extends Resource` in `texture_viewport_class.gd` (the name of the derived class doesn't matter) should make both messages print, which it doesn't.

That said, I cannot get it to work the "proper" way when I tried adding the following function into your `node.gd`

```GDScript
func _ready():
	var vt = ViewportTextureClass.new()
	print(vt.resource_local_to_scene)
	vt.resource_local_to_scene = true
	test2 = vt.duplicate()
	print(test2.resource_local_to_scene)
```

This prints `true\ntrue` but `_setup_local_to_scene()` is not called when it should be.

When I change the base from `ViewportTexture` to `Texture2D`, the result is `false\ntrue`, since the documentation says that a `ViewportTexture` is always `resource_local_to_scene=true`.  I cannot see how to initialize that value to true in the derived class at the startup, hence the effort of setting and _then_ duplicating it.  Also, the `resource_local_to_scene` doesn't make a difference when you define a member variable in the `ViewportTextureClass`, this is always unique.

So a lot more questions than answers, I'm afraid.  I'm here because I'm going to submit a bug to do with the `ViewportTexture`.

> I'm not sure the call to `_setup_local_to_scene()` should be happening anyway because you're not instantiating anything. Sometimes when I was working on this, that print statement stopped happening and I needed begin again with a fresh copy of your mrp project.

When launching the game you are instantiating the scene and all node/resources associated.

> If what you were doing was right, then changing the `extends ViewportTexture` to `extends Resource` in `texture_viewport_class.gd` (the name of the derived class doesn't matter) should make both messages print, which it doesn't.

Actually this isn't showing for a different reasons which is kind hidden. When changing the extends part you are assuming that all instance of this class will now extend resource and not extend ViewportTexture anymore. Unfortunately the resource are not changed, they would still be of type of ViewportTexture with a script that now extends Resource.

The method `setup_local_to_scene` outside of editor basically only gets called in `SceneState::instantiate(GenEditState p_edit_state)` so it should work fine. So to see if `setup_local_to_scene` works you can only use packed scene instantiation as it is the only place it gets called during runtime.

After checking it looks like `ViewportTexture` doesn't call base `Resource`'s `setup_local_to_scene` after overriding it. Or it doesn't call script's override with `GDVIRTUAL_CALL(_setup_local_to_scene);` in place of a base `Resource`. Not sure which is more appropriate here.
